findings.title: Missing Dependency Version Strategy and Package Availability
findings.description: Design references ioredis or redis npm packages but neither is installed in apps/api/package.json. No version pinning strategy or justification for package choice is documented.
findings.impact: Implementer must guess which library to use; potential for unresolved transitive dependencies or version conflicts.
findings.concrete_fix: Explicitly pin 'ioredis@^5.3.0' in apps/api/package.json with rationale: 'Official maintainer, TypeScript support, connection pooling for NestJS.' Document decision in design Section 2.

findings.title: Undefined CricketDataConfig Type and Configuration Flow
findings.description: Design references CricketDataConfig in multiple places (service constructors, module factory) but never defines the type. No interface, no relation to envSchema, no DI strategy documented.
findings.impact: Service and module instantiation will fail at runtime; DI resolution incomplete; config flow is broken.
findings.concrete_fix: Define CricketDataConfig interface in cricket-data/types/cricket-data.types.ts. Add toCricketDataConfig(env: Env) function to map environment variables to config. Add provider in cricket-data.module.ts using useFactory. Update Section 3.8 to show the complete config flow.

findings.title: Unvalidated Assumption: Player ID 1:1 Mapping Without Error Handling
findings.description: Design assumes database player IDs match provider IDs directly, with no mapping table or cross-validation. If IDs diverge (e.g., 'player-uuid-123' in DB vs 'espn-456' in provider), the endpoint silently falls back to stale cache with no actionable error message.
findings.impact: Runtime errors masked by generic 'Provider unavailable' message. User cannot distinguish between provider actually down vs. player not found in provider. Silent data corruption or missing stats.
findings.concrete_fix: Add error handling in PlayerStatsService.getPlayerStats(): catch CricketDataError with code INVALID_PLAYER and return database stats only (graceful degradation). Log with 'Provider does not have stats for player X; returning database metadata only'. Document that 1:1 mapping is assumed; ProviderPlayerMapping table is future work. Add test case for player found in DB but not in provider.

findings.title: Ambiguous Rate-Limit Backoff Coordination in Clustered Deployments
findings.description: Design stores rate-limit state in in-memory Map, which is not shared across API instances. Each instance independently detects rate-limits, causing duplicate retry storms at scale.
findings.impact: In production with N instances, provider receives N*3 retry attempts on rate-limit, risking provider account suspension. Acknowledged in Requirements but not solved in design.
findings.concrete_fix: Reuse CacheService (Redis or memory) for rate-limit coordination: check rateLimitCache.exists(rateLimitKey) before calling provider; on 429, store in rateLimitCache with TTL matching X-RateLimit-Reset. Document: 'Rate-limit backoff is shared across instances via Redis cache; in-memory cache provides per-instance tracking in development.'

findings.title: Stale Cache Data Age Is Never Communicated to Frontend
findings.description: Backend returns isCached: true but does not indicate how stale the data is. Frontend component cannot distinguish between 1-minute-old cache and 23-hour-old stale fallback.
findings.impact: User sees 'Cached • 2 hours ago' and cannot tell if data is recent or dangerously stale. Requirement 8.3 to 'display stale-data warning' is unimplementable.
findings.concrete_fix: Add fields to CacheMetadata: ageSeconds (time since fetch), isStale (true if expired cache). Backend populates when returning stale cache. Frontend displays 'Warning: Data is 5 hours old' badge when isStale=true and ageSeconds > threshold (e.g., 1800s).

findings.title: No Error Recovery for Malformed Provider Responses
findings.description: Design maps ESPN responses with no validation or schema enforcement. Malformed responses (missing playerId, invalid format) are cached as-is, causing frontend errors.
findings.impact: Invalid or partial data corrupts the cache and frontend rendering. No clear error message or fallback.
findings.concrete_fix: Add Zod validation schema for ESPN responses (espnPlayerStatsSchema). Validate before mapping. Throw CricketDataError with code PROVIDER_ERROR on validation failure. Document: 'All provider responses are validated against a schema before caching; malformed responses are treated as PROVIDER_ERROR and trigger fallback.'

findings.title: Module Factory Does Not Validate CricketDataConfig at Startup
findings.description: Module factory does not validate CricketDataConfig at application startup. Invalid configuration (bad URLs, unknown providers) fails lazily on first request.
findings.impact: App boots successfully with broken config; errors occur only when cricket data is first accessed, complicating debugging in production.
findings.concrete_fix: Add validateCricketConfig(config) function; call in module onModuleInit() lifecycle hook. Validate: provider name is known, URLs are valid, TTL values are reasonable. Fail fast with clear error message.

findings.title: RateLimitInfo Type Is Never Defined
findings.description: RateLimitInfo type is referenced but not defined in the design.
findings.impact: Implementation cannot create RateLimitInfo objects; TypeScript compilation fails.
findings.concrete_fix: Define RateLimitInfo interface in cricket-data/types/cricket-data.types.ts: { retryCount: number; nextRetryAt: Date; resetAt?: Date; endpointUrl: string }

findings.title: ESPNDataProvider isHealthy() Implementation Details Missing
findings.description: Design requires isHealthy() method but does not specify what constitutes a healthy provider or how to check.
findings.impact: Implementer must guess; may implement inefficient or incorrect health checks.
findings.concrete_fix: Document: 'isHealthy() attempts a lightweight HEAD request to {baseUrl}/status with 5s timeout. Returns true if status is 2xx; false otherwise. If ESPN does not expose /status, check with a known player search query.'

findings.title: SearchPlayers Pagination Offset Parameter Not Documented
findings.description: Component increments offset by fixed limit (10) but does not handle user-configurable limit. Future-proofing unclear.
findings.impact: If limit is later made configurable, pagination breaks.
findings.concrete_fix: Document: 'Pagination is controlled by offset and limit parameters. limit is fixed at 10 for initial CricketSearch component (future: make configurable). offset is incremented by limit on Load more. Results include hasMore flag to disable Load more when at end.'
